Timeline::set_day¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline Timeline::set_day(int day) const

Replace The Day Within Each Month¶

set_day() creates a new Timeline whose defined elements use day as their local day-of-month. It retains each element’s year, month, clock fields, nanoseconds, and timezone. It also retains the receiver’s rank and shape.

Use it for a calendar rule such as “place each timestamp on the first day of its existing month.” Do not use it to move forward or backward by a number of days: replacement does not carry across month boundaries.

Example: Normalize To The First Day¶

const auto t = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-01-15T23:58:59.123456789Z", "2024-06-20T04:05:06.000000004Z"},
    {"2024-09-28T12:30:45.900000000Z", "2024-12-01T00:00:00.000000001Z"},
});

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(t.set_day(1), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["2024-01-01T23:58:59.123456789+00:00", "2024-06-01T04:05:06.000000004+00:00"], 
  ["2024-09-01T12:30:45.900000000+00:00", "2024-12-01T00:00:00.000000001+00:00"]
]

Every element keeps its own year and month. Only the day field is shared. Calling set_day(1) is therefore different from flooring to one common date.

Month Length Is Checked Per Element¶

The argument must first lie in [1, 31]. It must then form a valid date with every defined element’s retained year and month. This second check matters for mixed-month timelines:

try {
  const auto months = pluss::timeline::make({
      "2024-01-10T00:00:00Z",
      "2024-02-10T00:00:00Z",
  });
  (void)months.set_day(30);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "day is not valid for every month\n";
}

Output¶

day is not valid for every month

January could accept day 30, but February 2024 cannot. The method returns no partial result. It never rolls into March and never clamps to month end.

Absent And Empty Timelines¶

NaT stays NaT; there is no calendar date to edit. An empty timeline returns an empty timeline with the same shape and timezone for valid arguments. The argument range is still checked on empty input, so empty.set_day(0) throws rather than hiding a programming error.

Timezone Consequences¶

Replacement occurs in the current local calendar. If the new local date and retained clock land in a daylight-saving gap, the method throws. If they land in an overlap, the first occurrence is selected. Convert to the intended timezone before calling set_day() whenever calendar boundaries are local.
